summary: Bidia Dandaron worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Saint Petersburg State University of Civil Aviation, the University of Saint Petersburg under Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov, and under Lubsan Sandan Tsydenov, later serving at the IMBTS from 1957.

Bimal Krishna Matilal was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Central Calcutta College, Sanskrit College, University of Calcutta, and Harvard under Quine and Føllesdal. He held posts at Toronto (~1968–1976), All Souls (1976), and Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was an Indologist and historian. He earned his MA at Patna University and his PhD at SOAS, University of London, under Lionel David Barnett. He taught at Patna College, headed a department at Patna University, and served at KPJRI.

Bing Chen is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a professorship at Sichuan University from around 1987 and was attested as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences in 1993.

Bintao Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ma completed an MA at Peking University in 2008 and earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha worked in Indology and anthropology. He studied at Scottish Church College, University of Calcutta, and Harvard University. He held positions at the Zoological Survey of India, Harvard, and directed the Anthropological Survey of India (1945–1954).

Birgit Kellner specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied under Muni Jambuvijaya and earned her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. Her career includes posts at the University of Vienna and leading the IKGA (2017–2023).

Bisheshwar Nath Reu was an Indologist and historian who studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. He headed the Archaeological Survey of India, the Government Museum Jodhpur, and the Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre, and served at Sumer Public Library (1933).
Biswanath Banerjee was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991 and served as president of The Asiatic Society around 2005 to 2007.

Blain Auer is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history. He was attested as a professor at the University of Lausanne in 2018 and has served on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.
Bo Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jiang earned a PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2008).

Bo Utas specializes in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University (~1958–1973) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander, later holding a post at Uppsala University from around 1987 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Han held a professorship at Dongguk University, where posts are attested in 2004 and 2015.

Bokar Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1959–1989) and was based at Bokar Ngedon Choekhor Ling Monastery from around 1984 to 2004.

Bong Seok Joo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Joo completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster and Ding-hwa E. Hsieh, followed by a PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser and Jacqueline I. Stone.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Chung earned a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and held faculty appointments in philosophy at Florida International University (1991–1992, attested 2012).

Boris Turayev was a historian who studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (~1887–1891). He later held academic posts at Imperial St. Petersburg University and the University of Saint Petersburg (~1898–1920).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1921–1925) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1933).

Boris Vladimirtsov studied at St. Petersburg University (~1904–1908) and under Antoine Meillet (~1911–1912). Working in linguistics, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1918–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).
Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Shri Singha Shedra under the traditional teachers Tubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam.
